function.mechanism: Lowers food pH and contributes tartness; phosphate species can also act as sequestrants/synergists that influence formulation stability.
common_food_categories: cola and other acidic soft drinks
food categories where phosphates are technologically needed for acidification/stabilization

adi.basis: EFSA 2019 group ADI for phosphorus from phosphates (including E338), expressed as phosphorus.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation set a group ADI of 40 mg phosphorus/kg bw/day and identified exceedance scenarios mainly in infants/toddlers and some brand-loyal high consumers.

adi.basis: JECFA chemical record reports group MTDI 70 mg/kg bw (as phosphorus) for phosphorus from all sources.

concerns.summary: A case-control study reported higher CKD odds with drinking two or more colas/day (colas contain phosphoric acid); non-cola carbonated beverages were not associated.
A 2024 randomized cross-over trial in healthy adults found that meals with inorganic phosphate additives altered acute calcium-phosphate homeostasis compared with comparator meals.
Recent CKD-focused review literature links higher inorganic phosphate intake (including additives) with pathways relevant to vascular calcification and cardiovascular risk in CKD populations.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA and JECFA both provide quantitative intake thresholds for phosphate exposure rather than concluding outright prohibition.
FDA lists phosphoric acid as GRAS in 21 CFR 182.1073 under good manufacturing practice conditions.
No IARC monograph classification entry for phosphoric acid was identified in the current IARC classification dataset reviewed.

populations: children and adolescents in brand-loyal/high-consumer scenarios
people with CKD or impaired phosphate handling
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported exceedance of the 40 mg phosphorus/kg bw/day group ADI in some high-exposure scenarios, especially younger age groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulators continue to allow E338, but EFSA set a finite group ADI and documented exceedance in vulnerable/high-consuming younger populations; human mechanistic and observational literature provides additional concern signals at higher inorganic phosphate intakes.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 group ADI: 40 mg phosphorus/kg bw/day
EFSA exceedance scenarios in infants/toddlers/high consumers
FDA GRAS status with GMP condition in 21 CFR 182.1073
JECFA group MTDI 70 mg/kg bw (as phosphorus)
No IARC classification entry for phosphoric acid in reviewed list
